The '''Chelsea F.C.–Tottenham Hotspur F.C. rivalry''' is a rivalry between London-based professional [[association football]] clubs [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. Chelsea play their home games at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]], while Tottenham Hotspur play their home games at the [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium]]. {{As of|October 2026}}, 182 competitive games have been played between the two teams, 83 of which were won by Chelsea and 56 by Spurs.

Although both teams have played against each other since the early 20th century, the rivalry between Chelsea and Tottenham did not begin until the [[1967 FA Cup final]], the first all-London FA Cup final. Chelsea fans consider Tottenham to be one of their rivals alongside [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|Arsenal]], [[West London derby|Fulham]] and [[Chelsea F.C.–Leeds United F.C. rivalry|Leeds United]], while Tottenham fans consider their rivalry with Chelsea to be secondary to that with [[North London derby|Arsenal]]. Many encounters between the two teams have been highly intense, including a match dubbed the 'Battle of the Bridge' in 2016.

==Background==
While Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur never considered each other primary rivals, there has always been strong needle between the fans dating back to the [[1967 FA Cup final]]. Matches between the two teams would often attract large attendances and would sometimes end up in [[hooliganism|violent clashes]] between supporters.

A 2012 survey has shown that Chelsea fans consider Tottenham to be their main rival, above [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. In the same survey, it is shown that Tottenham fans still consider Chelsea their second rival, below Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thedaisycutter.co.uk/2012/09/football-rivalries-the-survey/|title=Football Rivalries: The Survey|work=The Daisy Cutter|date=14 September 2012 |access-date=14 September 2012}}</ref> The 2004 film ''[[The Football Factory (film)|The Football Factory]]'' depicted scenes of the two teams' fans violently clashing.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kelso |first1=Paul |title=Just when football needed it least, films revive the spectre of hooligan gangs |url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2004/may/04/film.football |website=The Guardian |date=4 May 2004|access-date=16 March 2024}}</ref>

==History==
===Early matches===
The first league meeting between the two teams took place on 18 December 1909 at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] as Tottenham only joined the Football League in 1908 and won promotion to the [[Football League First Division]] in 1909. The match was won by Chelsea 2–1.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea v Tottenham Hotspur, 18 December 1909 |url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/chelsea-v-tottenham-hotspur-18-december-1909-58269/ |website=11v11.com |access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref> Both teams however struggled in the [[1909–10 Football League|1909–10 season]], and they met again at [[White Hart Lane]] on 30 April 1910 in the final match of season, with both fighting for survival in Division One. Spurs beat Chelsea 2–1, sending Chelsea down, with the winning goal scored by former Chelsea player [[Percy Humphreys]].<ref>{{cite book |title=The Biography of Tottenham Hotspur |first=Julie|last=Welch |chapter=Chapter 5: The Human Chain of Lightning |publisher=Vision Sports Publishing|date= 7 September 2015 |isbn= 9781909534506}}</ref>

===Start of rivalry===
The rivalry between the two teams dates back to the [[1967 FA Cup final]], which was the competition's first final to be contested between two teams from London, and is thus often dubbed the "Cockney Cup Final". Tottenham won the game 2–1 with over 100,000 people in attendance.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Davies |first1=Matt |title='The Cockney Cup Final' – When Tottenham and Chelsea's fierce rivalry began |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/tottenham-chelsea-rivalry-began-fa-cup-final-1967-a4446141.html |website=Evening Standard |access-date=28 November 2020 |language=en |date=20 May 2020}}</ref>

The rivalry was further ignited during the [[1974–75 Football League First Division|1974–75 season]], one in which Tottenham and Chelsea fought out a bitter battle against relegation from the First Division. Before the match, Tottenham were in the relegation zone and Chelsea were one point ahead of them. The tension of the match led to fans invading and fighting on the pitch before the game started.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://en.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/127460.html |title=Spurs v Chelsea crackers |first=Robin|last=Hackett |date=22 December 2011 |website=ESPN|access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref> After a delayed start, Tottenham won the game 2–0.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2016/11/throwback-thursday-tottenham-vs-chelsea-april-19th.html |title=Throwback Thursday: Tottenham vs Chelsea (April 19th, 1975) |first=James |last=Bridget Gordon |date=24 November 2016 |work=Paste Magazine |access-date=9 June 2019 |archive-date=9 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190609132731/https://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2016/11/throwback-thursday-tottenham-vs-chelsea-april-19th.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Chelsea failed to win either of their remaining two games and were ultimately relegated from the First Division with Tottenham staying up via a solitary point.<ref>{{cite web |title=First Division Table 1974/1975 |url=http://stats.football.co.uk/league_tables/1974_1975/first_division/index.shtml |website=stats.football.co.uk |access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref>

===1990–2015===
Chelsea became dominant in the meetings with Tottenham in the 1990s; starting from December 1990 they were unbeaten by their rivals for over a decade, including a 6–1 win at White Hart Lane in the 1997–98 season.<ref>{{cite web |first=Ryan|last=Kelly |title=Tottenham vs Chelsea London derby: History, games & players who played for both clubs |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/tottenham-vs-chelsea-london-derby-history-games-players-who/xajnbyec4o2s1at4t59jly1c7 |website=goal.com |access-date=5 June 2019 |language=en |date=16 August 2017}}</ref> On 5 November 2006, Tottenham beat Chelsea 2–1 at White Hart Lane, ending a 16-year period without victory against the Blues in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/nov/06/match.sport15|title=Terry sees red as Lennon ends Tottenham's 16-year hoodoo|first=Kevin|last=McCarra|work=The Guardian|access-date=28 November 2020|date=6 November 2006}}</ref> Spurs did, however, beat Chelsea in 2002 during a 5–1 win in the second leg of the league cup after a 2–1 defeat at Stamford Bridge, resulting in an aggregate score of 6–3.<ref>{{cite web |title=Spurs trounce Chelsea |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/worthington_cup/1775821.stm |website=BBC Sport |access-date=24 October 2020 |date=23 January 2002}}</ref>

On 11 March 2007, Chelsea and Tottenham met in the FA Cup quarter-finals, with Chelsea coming to 3–3 down from 1–3 and earning a replay. The next day, hooligans of Tottenham and Chelsea clashed in the streets of London, a fight in which 10 fans were knifed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/10-fans-knifed-in-chelsea-battle-7210890.html|title=10 fans knifed in Chelsea battle|work=Evening Standard|date=12 March 2007|first=Richard|last=Edwards|access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref> Chelsea eventually won the replay by 2–1, progressing in the semi-finals. In the next season, the two sides met in the [[2008 Football League Cup final]], with Tottenham winning the trophy after a 2–1 victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/7256729.stm|title=Tottenham 2–1 Chelsea|date=24 February 2008|access-date=21 August 2017|website=BBC Sport|first=Jonathan|last=Stevenson}}</ref>

Prior to signing for Chelsea in 2013, [[Willian (footballer, born 1988)|Willian]] had attracted interest from Tottenham. He completed a medical at Tottenham before meeting with Chelsea, which caused confusion as to which club he would sign for. Willian claims Chelsea was his first preference and he would have only signed with Tottenham if the deal with Chelsea fell through.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/aug/23/tottenham-chelsea-willian |title=Tottenham express outrage after Chelsea hijack Willian transfer |last1=Steinberg |first1=Jacob |last2=Hytner |first2=David |date=23 August 2013 |newspaper=The Guardian |access-date=31 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/willian-finally-reveals-secrets-of-tottenham-transfer-saga-i-was-stuck-in-their-office-for-8-hours_sto6877483/story.shtml |title=Willian reveals secrets of Tottenham transfer saga: 'I was stuck in their office for 8 hours' |date=7 August 2018 |website=Eurosport |access-date=31 May 2022}}</ref> It is alleged that during [[Roman Abramovich]]'s tenure as Chelsea owner, he refused to do any business with Tottenham.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keighley |first=Freddie |date=6 September 2020 |title=Roman Abramovich told Chelsea players he 'doesn't do business' with Tottenham |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/roman-abramovich-chelsea-players-tottenham-22636860 |access-date=14 August 2022 |website=The Mirror|language=en}}</ref>

On 1 March 2015, Chelsea won the [[2015 Football League Cup final]] 2–0 against Tottenham, with goals provided by [[John Terry]] and [[Diego Costa]]. Chelsea fans made headlines for racist and anti-Semitic chants on [[London Underground|the Underground]] after the match.<ref>{{cite web |title=Footage of Chelsea fans singing 'racist' songs emerges |url=https://www.itv.com/news/2015-03-06/footage-of-chelsea-fans-singing-racist-songs-emerges |website=ITV News |access-date=22 January 2021 |date=6 March 2015}}</ref> After this final, Chelsea surpassed Tottenham in number of trophies won.{{citation needed|date=November 2020}}

===2016: 'Battle of the Bridge'===
{{see also|2015–16 Chelsea F.C. season|2015–16 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season}}
[[File:Chelsea v Spurs 2 May 2016 - players scuffling.jpg|thumb|Scuffling between players at the match between Chelsea and Spurs dubbed the 'Battle of Stamford Bridge' on 2 May 2016.]]
In the [[2015–16 Premier League|2015–16 season]], Tottenham's league performance improved under their manager [[Mauricio Pochettino]], and they were a contender for the title. Chelsea on the other hand had their [[2015–16 Chelsea F.C. season|worst season]] in 20 years which saw their manager [[José Mourinho]] sacked after a bad start to the season.<ref name="skysports battle">{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/story-telling/11095/12670117/the-battle-of-the-bridge-chelsea-and-tottenhams-infamous-match-revisited |title= The Battle of the Bridge |first=Joe |last=Shread |work=Sky Sports|access-date=17 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220821044734/https://www.skysports.com/football/story-telling/11095/12670117/the-battle-of-the-bridge-chelsea-and-tottenhams-infamous-match-revisited|archive-date=21 August 2022}}</ref> Tottenham headed into the match against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on 2 May 2016, a match that Tottenham needed to win to have a chance at winning the league. The encounter proved to be an ill-tempered match, which would later be called the 'Battle of Stamford Bridge' or 'Battle of the Bridge'.<ref name="skysports battle"/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2016/nov/25/mauricio-pochettino-battle-of-stamford-bridge-tottenham-chelsea |title=Battle of Stamford Bridge: Tottenham return to the scene of their undoing |first=David|last=Hytner|date=25 November 2016 |work=The Guardian|access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/tottenham-matured-in-battle-of-the-bridge-defeat-against-chelsea-mauricio-pochettino-z8fbqrv09 |title=Tottenham matured in 'Battle of the Bridge' defeat against Chelsea – Mauricio Pochettino|first=Jon|last=West|date=7 January 2019|work=The Times|access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref>

Tottenham took the lead with two goals scored by [[Harry Kane]] and [[Son Heung-min]]. In the second half, [[Gary Cahill]] and [[Eden Hazard]] scored the two goals for Chelsea. It ended as a 2–2 draw which automatically gave [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] their first ever Premier League title.<ref>{{cite web|first=Aimee|last=Lewis |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36126924 |title=Chelsea 2–2 Tottenham Hotspur |website=BBC Sport |date=2 May 2016 |access-date=27 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35988673 |title=Leicester City win Premier League title after Tottenham draw at Chelsea |website=BBC Sport |date=2 May 2016|access-date=27 November 2016}}</ref> This was arguably the closest Tottenham had come to winning the league since their last title in 1961 and since their last third-place finish in 1990. The match saw many altercations between players and benches on and off the field, especially after Hazard scored the equalising and final goal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Danny Rose: Tottenham defender apologises for ugly scenes at Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36190716|access-date=17 October 2025|website=BBC Sport|date=3 May 2016}}</ref> [[Mark Clattenburg]], who refereed the game, subsequently stated that he could have "sent three players off from Tottenham" but chose instead to allow them to play on, giving the team a total of nine [[Penalty card#Yellow card|yellow card]]s (a Premier League record for any team), so as to allow them to "self destruct" and have no one else to blame but themselves.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mark Clattenburg: I allowed Tottenham to self-destruct against Chelsea in 2016 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42219327 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=17 October 2025 |date=4 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mark Clattenburg took a 'gamble too far' - Dermot Gallagher |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42234221 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=17 October 2025 |date=5 December 2017}}</ref> There were also three yellow cards for Chelsea, and [[Mousa Dembélé (Belgian footballer)|Mousa Dembélé]] received a six-match suspension for violent conduct.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36229203 |title= Mousa Dembele: Tottenham midfielder gets six-game ban for violent conduct |website=BBC Sport |date=6 May 2016|access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref> As a result, both clubs had to face three FA charges and they were fined for failing to control their players.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2016/05/16/chelsea-and-tottenham-fined-total-of-600000-by-fa-after-stamford/|title=Chelsea and Tottenham fined total of £600,000 by FA after Stamford Bridge chaos|date=16 May 2016|access-date=21 August 2017|newspaper=The Telegraph|first=Jeremy|last=Wilson}}</ref>

===2017–present===
[[File:Chelsea 4 Spurs 2 (33405169703).jpg|thumb|Chelsea and Tottenham players before the FA Cup semi-final in 2017.]]
On 4 January 2017, Tottenham beat Chelsea 2–0 at White Hart Lane, ending Chelsea's record 13-game winning streak in the Premier League.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/38447903|title=Tottenham Hotspur 2–0 Chelsea|date=4 January 2017|access-date=29 May 2018|website=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=McNulty}}</ref> It brought Tottenham to within five points of Chelsea, who were leading the Premier League. Tottenham and Chelsea then went on to be the two title rivals in what was a two-horse race for the title, in which Chelsea eventually prevailed with 93 points to Tottenham's 86 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/national/england/premier-league/20162017/regular-season/r35992/|title=2016–17 Premier League table|access-date=29 May 2018|publisher=Soccerway}}</ref> Tottenham also lost to Chelsea in the FA Cup [[2016–17 FA Cup#Semi-finals|semi-final]] in the same season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39604653|title=Chelsea 4–2 Tottenham Hotspur|date=22 April 2017|access-date=29 May 2018|website=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=McNulty}}</ref>

On 20 August 2017, Tottenham and Chelsea met early in the [[2017–18 Premier League]] season, with Tottenham playing their first-ever home Premier League match at [[Wembley Stadium]]. Chelsea won the match 2–1 with two goals scored by [[Marcos Alonso Mendoza|Marcos Alonso]], ending Tottenham's 19-game home Premier League unbeaten run.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/40914668|title=Tottenham Hotspur 1–2 Chelsea|date=20 August 2017|access-date=21 August 2017|website=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=McNulty}}</ref> In the same season on 1 April 2018, Tottenham won away to Chelsea 3–1, with goals from [[Dele Alli]] and [[Christian Eriksen]]. This was Tottenham's first win in 28 years at Stamford Bridge.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/tottenham-mauricio-pochettino-praises-fighter-dele-alli-star-states-england-case-chelsea-brace-a3803711.html |title=Mauricio Pochettino praises 'fighter' Dele Alli as Tottenham star states England case with Chelsea brace |first=Jack|last= Rosser |date= 1 April 2018 |work=Evening Standard|access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref>

On 22 December 2019, Chelsea played their first match at Tottenham's [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium|new stadium]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Match report: Tottenham 0 Chelsea 2 |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/12/22/match-report--tottenham-vs-chelsea |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |access-date=23 December 2019 |date=22 December 2019}}</ref> The match, which Chelsea won 2–0 with a brace by Willian, received wide media coverage due to alleged racist behaviour by Tottenham fans, aimed at Chelsea's defender [[Antonio Rüdiger]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50797989|title=Tottenham Hotspur 0–2 Chelsea|date=22 December 2019|access-date=23 December 2019|website=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=McNulty}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea win at Tottenham marred as Rudiger suffers racist abuse |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=541667 |website=ESPN |access-date=23 December 2019 |language=en |date=22 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea's Antonio Rudiger alleges he was racially abused by Tottenham fans |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11893597/chelseas-antonio-rudiger-allegedly-racially-abused-during-tottenham-game |website=Sky Sports |access-date=23 December 2019 |language=en |date=23 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200314205755/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11893597/chelseas-antonio-rudiger-allegedly-racially-abused-during-tottenham-game|archive-date=14 March 2020}}</ref> A Chelsea supporter was also arrested for alleged racist abuse against Spurs player [[Son Heung-min]], who was sent off for kicking Rüdiger after he fouled Son.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/dec/23/chelsea-supporter-arrested-for-racially-abusing-tottenhams-son-heung-min |title=Chelsea supporter arrested for allegedly racially abusing Son Heung-min |first=Jacob |last=Steinberg|date= 23 December 2019|work=The Guardian|access-date=23 December 2019}}</ref> It led to a call for government action on racism in football.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50893279 |title=Government prepared to take 'further steps' over racism in football |date=23 December 2019 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=24 December 2019}}</ref> However, no evidence of racist abuse against Rüdiger was found after a police investigation.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/jan/06/tottenham-investigation-finds-no-evidence-of-alleged-racism-against-chelseas-rudiger |title=Investigation finds 'no evidence' of alleged racism against Chelsea's Rüdiger |first=Ed |last=Aarons|date=6 January 2020|work=The Guardian|access-date=6 January 2020}}</ref>

On 5 January 2022, Chelsea took on Tottenham in the [[2021–22 EFL Cup|League Cup]] semi-final first leg at Stamford Bridge, and won the match 2–0.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Chelsea 2–0 Tottenham Hotspur: Blues win Carabao Cup semi-final first leg|language=en-GB|website=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59814563|access-date=18 March 2022|date=5 January 2022|first=Begley|last=Begley}}</ref> A week later, Chelsea again beat Tottenham 1–0 in the second leg, booking a spot at Wembley for the [[2022 EFL Cup final|final]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Carabao Cup semi-final second leg: Tottenham Hotspur 0–1 Chelsea (0–3 agg)|language=en-GB|website=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59876396|access-date=18 March 2022|date=12 January 2022|first=Phil|last=McNulty}}</ref> On 23 January, Chelsea faced Tottenham again in a 2–0 win in the Premier League.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Spurs, 2021/22 {{!}} Premier League|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66564|access-date=18 March 2022|website=premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> The win meant that Chelsea had beaten Tottenham three times in the space of a month—the last Premier League team to achieve this feat was [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] against [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] in January 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea vs Tottenham: Premier League preview, team news, stats, predictions, kick-off time, live on Sky|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12521054/chelsea-vs-tottenham-premier-league-preview-team-news-stats-predictions-kick-off-time-live-on-sky|access-date=18 March 2022|website=Sky Sports|language=en|date=23 January 2022}}</ref>

A Premier League match at Stamford Bridge on 14 August 2022 was notable for having both Chelsea's manager [[Thomas Tuchel]] and Spurs manager [[Antonio Conte]], who previously managed Chelsea, sent off. This followed multiple altercations between them on the touchline, initially when Conte celebrated in front of Tuchel following a Spurs equaliser, and later when both managers clashed whilst shaking hands after the final whistle.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Chelsea 2–2 Tottenham Hotspur: Thomas Tuchel & Antonio Conte sent off after late equaliser|first=Phil|last=McNulty|language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62453943 |access-date=14 August 2022|date=14 August 2022}}</ref> The match resulted in a 2–2 draw following a 96th minute equaliser from Spurs striker Kane.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 2–2 Tottenham: Antonio Conte and Tuchel Tuchel sent off after Harry Kane's last-gasp equaliser |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12672334/chelsea-2-2-tottenham-antonio-conte-and-tuchel-tuchel-sent-off-after-harry-kanes-last-gasp-equaliser |website=Sky Sports |access-date=14 August 2022 |language=en |date=14 August 2022}}</ref>

The Premier League clash between the two teams that took place on 6 November 2023 has been described as "chaotic",<ref name="bbc 7 nov 2023">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67340076 |title=Tottenham 1–4 Chelsea: Unpacking nine VAR checks in chaotic half of football |work=BBC Sport |date=7 November 2023|access-date=7 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/nov/06/tottenhams-chaotic-derby-defeat-reveals-first-flaws-in-frantic-angeball |title=Tottenham's chaotic derby defeat reveals first flaws in frantic Angeball |first=Jacob |last=Steinberg |date=7 November 2023|access-date=7 November 2023|website=The Guardian}}</ref> "madness",<ref name="telegraph 7 november 2023">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2023/11/06/tottenham-vs-chelsea-premier-league-live-score-updates/|title= Tottenham's standing ovation after crushing Chelsea defeat summed up the madness|first=Jason |last=Burt|date=7 November 2023 |work=The Telegraph|access-date=7 November 2023}}</ref> and one of the "wildest", "most frenetic and mesmeric" games in Premier League history.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13002277/tottenham-vs-chelsea-the-wildest-first-half-in-premier-league-history |title=Tottenham vs Chelsea: The wildest game in Premier League history? |access-date=7 November 2023|work=Sky Sports|date=7 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/38834733/wild-spurs-chelsea-fracas-proves-angeball-here-stay |title=Wild Spurs-Chelsea fracas proves 'Angeball' is here to stay |first=James |last=Olley|website= ESPN |date=7 November 2023|access-date=7 November 2023}}</ref> The match saw the return of former Tottenham manager Pochettino to Tottenham Stadium as manager of Chelsea, and there were five disallowed goals (four in one half), six yellow cards (Tottenham's manager [[Ange Postecoglou]] received one), two Tottenham players sent off, and 11 major [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] checks, which added 21 minutes to the game in stoppage time.<ref name="bbc 7 nov 2023" /><ref name="telegraph 7 november 2023"/> It ended in 4–1 home defeat for Tottenham with [[Nicolas Jackson]] scoring a hat-trick, but the home team and manager Postecoglou still received a standing ovation from their fans at the end.<ref name="telegraph 7 november 2023"/>

==Players who have played for or managed both teams==
Below are the players and managers who played for or managed both clubs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Players who played for Tottenham Hotspur FC and Chelsea FC |url=https://fbref.com/en/friv/players-who-played-for-multiple-clubs-countries.fcgi |access-date=10 January 2024|website=FBref.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mumford |first=Robin |date=1 November 2023|title=14 best players who have played for both Chelsea and Tottenham |url=https://www.footballfancast.com/tottenham-hotspur-spurs-chelsea-played-for-both-premier-league/ |access-date=10 January 2024|website=Football FanCast|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=26 February 2023|title=From Glenn Hoddle to William Gallas – Meet the players who played for both Chelsea and Tottenham |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/from-glenn-hoddle-to-william-gallas-meet-the-players-who-played-for-both-chelsea-and-tottenham/blt8894c3c5a3cc944c |access-date=10 January 2024|website=goal.com |language=en|first=Mudeet|last=Arora}}</ref>
